name: Carol Whitmore

items.text: In June 2022, while running for county commission, Whitmore removed two of opponent Jason Bearden's campaign signs and turned them in to police. Bearden filed a criminal complaint. The State Attorney declined to charge her, saying the State could not prove criminal intent. She said she believed the signs were on private property or violated a city ordinance.
items.why: The prosecutor declined charges and made no finding of abuse of office, and a campaign-sign dispute has no clear bearing on the owner's criteria (including criterion 6).

for_review: The State Attorney's letter to the governor (whitmore_memo.pdf, linked from the Bradenton Times article) could not be opened, so the item rests on the news report. The Aug. 19, 2022 decision date is not stated in any page I read, so I left it out. The owner-sites search returned nothing about Whitmore. The Islander (Anna Maria) reported that she said at the police station she 'probably shouldn't have done that,' but I only saw that in a search snippet, so I left it out of the text. Her donor-related claims in a 2022 opponent TV ad (development money, 'rubber-stamped' projects) were not examined and are not an item here. Nothing was checked about her current city commissioner record.
